author: sonnet
label: seeded-06-01
changes: Spelled out the look-up branch for unknown email: send nothing and go to the generic response.
Defined the rate limit as per account, counted from reset_tokens rows in the last hour, with the over-limit behaviour.
Said the token holds the hash only and the raw token goes only into the emailed link.
Said the API adds a job to the queue and responds without waiting for the send.
Defined the token check (found, under 30 minutes, unused, not killed) and the single expired page for every invalid case.
Stated that the token is marked used only when the password is saved, inside one transaction, and that opening the link changes nothing.
Stated that a rejected password keeps the token valid for retry.
Defined revoke sessions as deleting all sessions rows for the account, including the resetter's, and gave the reason it comes before the confirmation email.
Wrote out the worker's retry behaviour (3 retries with backoff, then log and drop) and its effect on each email.
Added a short terms note for token and session.
Rate limit now states that dead and used tokens count too (Q10).
Terms: added reset_tokens, dead token and Email queue definitions, and said what a deleted session means for a device (Q11, Q15).
Create token is now one transaction; the email job is added after the commit (Q12).
Set password: marking the token used is now a conditional update, so a double submit rolls back and shows the expired page (Q14).
Set password: a transaction error rolls back, shows a retry message and leaves the token usable (Q13).
Confirmation email job is added after the commit; sessions are deleted in the same transaction as the password save.
Added a failure table covering token creation, queue add, send, set-password and confirmation email.
Added a short summary paragraph with how the existing system works today, and numbered the three flows.
Open questions now says the queue's location and durability are unknown (Q15).
Kept the diagram form; put the summary and the terms just before it and the notes just after it.
Opened with a short paragraph on how the existing system works today and why the API only queues mail.
Added a one-line Session definition saying that deleting the row logs the device out on its next request.
Defined the token, reset_tokens, dead token and Email queue in plain one-line terms.
Added the reason that the new link and the killing of old links happen in one transaction, so two live links never exist at once.
Stated that the rate limit is per account and not per IP.
Gave the reason for counting every reset_tokens row: each row was an email, and it stops new links from getting around the limit.
Stated that unknown addresses get the same message and nothing is sent to them.
Added the point that a logged-out device is rejected on its next request, and that the client's reaction is existing behaviour.
Merged the repeated retry and failure wording into the notes and the table.
Added two table rows: two submits at once, and a database error leaving old sessions alive.
Cut the repeated explanations of the generic response and of queue timing.

Checked the brief's fixed requirements against the first version and kept every one: 32-byte token, SHA-256, 30 minutes, once only, new link kills old, check at load and at submit, 12 characters plus breached list, retry allowed, log out all devices including the resetting one, confirmation email, redirect without auto login.
Left out the exact job format and the queue technology, which the plan does not need; the queue question stays in the open questions.
holes: Q15: What does the Email queue hold and where does it live? Is the job lost if the queue or worker is down when the API adds it? (author: The Email queue is part of the existing system and the brief does not say what technology backs it or where it lives. A job holds the recipient, which email to send, and for a reset the link with the raw token. Whether a job survives the queue or worker being down is not known. If adding the job fails, it is handled like Q12: the user simply requests another link. Added one line to the open questions.)
